title: Hina rendering performance
metricScope: Rendering performance measurements; no visual-quality or likeness score is inferred.

benchmarkHardware.graphicsBackend: ANGLE with Mesa OpenGL ES through EGL

method: One bounded active-turntable run at each canvas size, with 60 requestAnimationFrame-driven scene draws after 10 warmup frames. Wall-clock draw intervals and RAF timestamps were recorded separately. Five explicit drawScene plus 1×1 RGBA readPixels completions followed each cadence run.
resourceMethod: Aggregate CPU-time deltas for the isolated browser, divided by elapsed wall time; 100% means one CPU core. Aggregate resident memory can double-count shared pages.
limits: This is a short headless-browser measurement on the stated integrated GPU, not a measurement of physical phone hardware.
RAF cadence does not guarantee physical display presentation or refresh rate.
Actual framebuffer completion is reported separately from CPU draw submission.
Static geometry reuses its shadow map during orbit.
Concurrent system activity may affect a short run.
revisionNote: The bounded benchmark preceded the final small eye/collar, browser-portability, and preset-control refinements. The measurements were preserved without being rerun or relabeled after those edits.

softwareDiagnosis.conclusion: The initial review backend had multi-second completed-frame costs. Small submission timings were misleading for that workload. Native Intel EGL resolved the measured backend bottleneck.
softwareDiagnosis.note: These earlier software diagnostics are retained as context; software submission cadence is not presented as an achieved rendering frame rate.

reviewBrowserBehavior: Prefer a successfully probed native WebGL2 context; report a native failure before selecting a verified software fallback. An explicit software override is available.
